creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`crates/muster-seam/tests/` now holds eight files and eight `#[test]` functions, one each, and every one carries the same comment: the seam keeps its session in a process global, so a second test in the same binary would race the first. Adding a gesture therefore costs a new file and a new daemon, which is why `attach.rs` chains nine sub-scenarios through helpers instead.

The real cost is bisectability rather than coverage. A chained scenario aborts at the first failure, so the later behaviour never runs and one red CI run cannot say whether that broke too.

What it needs is a way to get a fresh session between tests - a reset entry point beside `muster_set_event_callback`, or a session handle the tests own rather than a global. `session.rs` holds twelve module statics plus `SESSION: LazyLock<Mutex<Session>>` and has no reset of any kind today, so this is a real refactor rather than a helper.

Split out of a_298rp2Pss, which took the other half (extending `--contract`, and the first gestures). Sequenced deliberately: slot 1's muster-CLI work rewrites `session.rs` heavily, and a structural change written against the current file would be written against a version about to be replaced. Worth picking up once that has landed.
title: 🧪 One test per binary is what stops the gesture tier growing
